title: WSUS · Patch and Recovery Operations
description: Configure a standalone WSUS pilot, approve updates, check reboots and practice recovery.
baseline: Standalone WSUS01 · lab.example.test · disposable Windows member server
prerequisite: Complete Install WSUS first. This class uses a standalone WSUS01 server, not the WSUS database/content managed by a MECM software update point. WSUS is deprecated but still supported in applicable Windows Server versions; learn the existing service and evaluate current alternatives for new designs.
supplies: WSUS01 with successful synchronization and only the required products selected.
DC01 for scoped Group Policy and one practice member-server pilot.
A verified recovery plan and an practice lab update/restart window.

lessons.title: Create WSUS Pilot and Rollout Groups
lessons.description: Separate one practice server into a pilot group before approving updates.
lessons.what: Separate one practice server into a pilot group before approving updates.
lessons.why: Approvals affect the selected group. A small pilot helps you catch problems before updating other servers.
needs: Complete the install and configuration lessons in this class first.
Use only the lab.example.test practice environment and practice test computers.
bestPractices: Keep pilot devices separate from all other computers. Record the starting state and check the actual result before expanding a deployment.
commonMistakes: Selecting All Systems instead of the named pilot collection or computer group.

troubleshooting.problem: The expected device or result is missing.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the target computer, its DNS and network access, then the matching client/server log named in the step. Stop before expanding the change.

lessons.pass: The standalone WSUS pilot group contains only APP01, which receives the correct WSUS policy.
lessons.exercise: Record the WSUS URL, pilot device and applied GPO without including credentials.

quiz.question: Where should you test this change first?
options: Only the named disposable pilot devices
quiz.explanation: A small pilot limits the effect of a mistake and gives you a result to check.

steps.title: Check your standalone WSUS server
actions: Open Server Manager → Tools → Windows Server Update Services. Expand WSUS01.
Select Options → Computers. For this first lab select Use the Update Services console, then Apply. This is server-side targeting; do not configure a client-side targeting GPO at the same time.
Select Options → Products and Classifications. Select only your supported lab Windows product and required classifications; avoid downloading every product.
steps.expected: The standalone WSUS server uses console-assigned groups and a limited product scope. This is WSUS01, not a MECM-managed software update point.

breakdown.meaning: A WSUS server controlled by MECM should be managed through Configuration Manager for update deployments. Do not apply this standalone approval steps to that server.

steps.title: Create the two computer groups
actions: Expand Computers → All Computers. Right-click All Computers → Add Computer Group.
Name the first group LAB-WSUS-Pilot. Create a second group named LAB-WSUS-Rollout.
Do not approve updates to All Computers while practicing. Keep the rollout group empty until the pilot is verified.
steps.expected: Both named groups exist under All Computers.

breakdown.meaning: This is a WSUS target list, separate from a MECM device collection.

screenshot.title: Interface reference: Add Computer Group in the WSUS Administration UI.
screenshot.instructions: Orientation reference for the named application, not a capture of every action. Follow the written lab.example.test values and check your own result.

steps.title: Point a practice client at WSUS
steps.where: DC01 · Group Policy Management, then APP01
actions: On DC01 open Group Policy Management. Create a GPO named LAB-WSUS-Clients and link it only to the OU containing your practice member-server client, not the Domain Controllers OU.

Edit Computer Configuration → Policies → Administrative Templates → Windows Components → Windows Update. Find Specify intranet Microsoft update service location (inside Manage updates offered from Windows Server Update Service on newer ADMX templates).

Enable it. Set both update and statistics URLs to the actual WSUS01 endpoint: http://WSUS01.lab.example.test:8530 only if that is your configured HTTP lab endpoint; use the verified HTTPS URL and port for a TLS-configured server.
Configure Automatic Updates for a lab schedule you can observe. On APP01 run gpupdate /force, then open Settings → Update & Security → Windows Update → Check for updates.
Back in WSUS, wait for APP01 to report. In Unassigned Computers, right-click APP01 → Change Membership and assign LAB-WSUS-Pilot.
steps.expected: APP01 reports to WSUS01 and belongs only to the intended pilot group. Group Policy results confirm the intranet update server setting.

breakdown.meaning: The client must know which update server to ask. A WSUS group alone does not configure the client.

lessons.why: A successful download is not proof of a healthy server after restart. Test its services before expanding the change.

steps.title: Prepare recovery and select an applicable update
actions: Check that APP01 is practice and has a tested recovery path appropriate for its workload. Record its current OS build and whether its test application responds.
In WSUS select Updates → All Updates. Filter Approval = Unapproved and Status = Needed. Refresh the view after synchronization.
Open the details for one supported update needed by APP01. Read its things to prepare, restart behavior and known issues on the linked Microsoft support page. Record the KB number.
steps.expected: A specific needed update and its recovery plan are recorded; no broad approval exists.

breakdown.meaning: WSUS reported that a client needs this update. Applicability and reporting can change after another update or restart.

steps.title: Approve the update only for the pilot
actions: Right-click the selected update → Approve. In the approval dialog set Install only for LAB-WSUS-Pilot.
Review inherited approvals and confirm All Computers and LAB-WSUS-Rollout are not receiving a new broad install approval from this action. Select OK.
On APP01 open Windows Update and check again. Install the offered update in the planned lab window. Save work and restart when required.
steps.expected: Only the pilot receives the new approval and APP01 completes the update/restart workflow.

breakdown.meaning: Approval makes an update available to its target group; the client policy and update state govern when it installs.

steps.title: Validate before expanding
steps.where: APP01 · Windows Update history; WSUS01 · reports
actions: On APP01 review Windows Update history, confirm the intended KB/build where applicable, and test the application and expected services.
In WSUS refresh APP01’s status after reporting. Compare the console status with the actual client result.

If the pilot is healthy, approve the same update for LAB-WSUS-Rollout only when you have additional practice clients. Schedule servers in batches with a health check after each batch; do not reboot redundant domain controllers together.
steps.expected: The pilot has a confirmed update result and application check before any rollout approval.

breakdown.meaning: Stop the rollout when the pilot fails. Keeping the rest of the group unchanged gives you time to investigate.

lessons.title: Troubleshoot WSUS and Recover a Failed Update
lessons.description: Follow a missing-client or failed-update problem from policy to logs, then choose a supported recovery action.
lessons.what: Follow a missing-client or failed-update problem from policy to logs, then choose a supported recovery action.
lessons.why: Changing approvals, uninstalling an update and restoring a server are different actions. Choose the action that addresses the evidence.

steps.title: Find why a client is missing
actions: Check the clock, DNS and WSUS endpoint. In PowerShell run gpresult /r /scope computer and confirm the intended GPO applies.

Check the effective intranet update server policy, then test the configured WSUS port with Test-NetConnection WSUS01.lab.example.test -Port 8530 for the HTTP example. Use your real TLS port if different.

Open Event Viewer → Applications and Services Logs → Microsoft → Windows → WindowsUpdateClient → Operational. Match errors to the time you checked for updates. Do not disable the firewall or delete SoftwareDistribution as the first response.
steps.expected: You have policy, connectivity and update event saved result for the named client.

breakdown.meaning: A missing console entry can come from policy, network access or reporting delays. Each requires a different fix.

screenshot.instructions: Orientation reference for the named application, not a capture of every action. Follow the written lab.example.test values and check your own result.

steps.title: Stop expansion and choose recovery
actions: If the pilot fails, stop new rollout approvals and record the affected KB, error and symptoms. An approval change does not uninstall an update that is already installed.
Read the KB’s known issues and supported removal/recovery guidance. Some updates cannot be uninstalled. Do not force removal or delete update files manually.

On the practice client only, use Windows Update history → Uninstall updates if the KB supports removal, then restart in the lab window. If removal is unsupported, use your tested workload-aware backup/rebuild plan.
steps.expected: The recovery decision follows the KB and the lab backup plan; no unsupported rollback has been forced.

breakdown.meaning: A supported uninstall may remove an update. A server restore or rebuild recovers a larger state and needs a separate tested plan.

steps.title: Check recovery and review WSUS health
actions: On APP01 repeat the original application, service and update-history checks. Save the new result and the incident timeline.

On WSUS01 review synchronization results and available disk space. Review Options → Server Cleanup Wizard before running it; choose only understood cleanup options and protect the WSUS database/content using your documented recovery plan.
Keep failed updates out of the rollout until you have a documented fix and a new successful pilot test.
steps.expected: The client’s service is restored or the remaining fault is clearly documented, and the rollout remains paused until a new pilot succeeds.

breakdown.meaning: Use the same application check from before patching. A running Windows desktop alone is not enough.
